intro.author: 'Simon Peter' (1:1), writing as his death approached (1:14). Its authorship was questioned even in the early church, and many modern scholars think a later follower wrote it in Peter's name; others defend Peter as the author.
intro.written: If by Peter, shortly before his death, about AD 64–68; scholars who doubt Peter's authorship date it later
intro.audience: Believers who 'have obtained like precious faith' (1:1); calling this the 'second epistle' (3:1) suggests the same readers as 1 Peter
intro.setting: False teachers had arisen among the believers, promising freedom while living immorally, and scoffing at the idea that Christ would return. Much of chapter 2 closely parallels the letter of Jude, and most scholars think one writer drew on the other. The letter reads like a farewell testament, reminding readers of what they already know.
intro.purpose: To urge believers to grow in their faith, to rely on the apostles' eyewitness testimony and the prophetic Scriptures, to reject false teachers, and to keep waiting for the day of the Lord.
intro.bigIdea: Grow in the knowledge of Christ and hold to the truth, because the Lord's promise is sure even when it seems delayed.

outline.title: Growing in faith; eyewitness and prophecy
The day of the Lord will come

commentary.t: THE SECOND EPISTLE GENERAL OF PETER
